translations.title: Your own numbers
translations.excerpt: Financial independence starts with knowing four figures that are yours alone.

blocks.text: Independence is not about separating from a partner or a family. It is about being able to answer four questions without asking anyone: what do I earn or control, what do I own, what do I owe, and what would I live on for six months if everything changed tomorrow.

items: Income you control: salary, business income, rent, or the household money that is yours to decide on.
Assets in your name: bank balances, deposits, gold, investments, property. Joint counts as half unless agreed otherwise.
Debts in your name or that you have guaranteed.
Your emergency months: liquid assets in your name divided by essential monthly expenses.

blocks.text: Three things to do this month

items: Open or revive a bank account solely in your name with net banking and UPI.
Check that you are the nominee on your partner's accounts and policies, and they on yours.
Keep copies of policies, property papers and account numbers somewhere you can reach alone.

blocks.text: Under Indian law, a wife's stridhan (gifts and earnings that are hers) remains hers through marriage, separation or widowhood. Keeping a record is what makes that right usable.

items: Four numbers: income, assets, debts, emergency months.
An account in your own name is the first step.

questions.q: Which of these is not one of the four numbers?
What is the first practical step toward financial independence?
options: Open an account solely in your name
